You allocate a higher tokens-per-minute (TPM) value to the model.  
  
What is the effect of this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Azure region availability of the model changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model generates shorter responses and additional source citations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The speed and scale at which the model deployment can process inputs changes.

definition.explanation:
A higher TPM allocation raises the deployment’s token rate limit, allowing it to handle more token processing and request volume per minute before throttling. It changes deployment throughput and scale, not regional availability or the model’s response characteristics.

**Learn more:** [Manage and increase quotas for resources with Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/quota) · [Manage Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry Models quota](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/how-to/quota?tabs=rest)

finalExplanation: A higher TPM allocation raises the deployment’s token rate limit, allowing it to handle more token processing and request volume per minute before throttling. It changes deployment throughput and scale, not regional availability or the model’s response characteristics.

definition.stemRaw:
You intend to deploy a generative AI model to a Microsoft Foundry project in the East US Azure region.  
  
What should you verify first?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Foundry model availability varies by provider, deployment type, and Azure region. A model must be available in East US before it can be deployed there; configuration details such as token limits, API support, and authentication do not overcome an unsupported regional deployment.

**Learn more:** [Feature availability across cloud regions - Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/reference/region-support) · [Deploy Microsoft Foundry Models in the Foundry portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/how-to/deploy-foundry-models)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Foundry model availability varies by provider, deployment type, and Azure region. A model must be available in East US before it can be deployed there; configuration details such as token limits, API support, and authentication do not overcome an unsupported regional deployment.

definition.stemRaw: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: An Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools analyzer returns results in the HTML format.
The Content Understanding REST API analyzes content synchronously and returns results in the same response.
Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools can extract structured information from documents, images, audio, and video files.

statements.text: Whisper models in Azure OpenAI are used to convert speech to text.
Embedding models in Azure OpenAI are used to convert text into numeric vectors.
GPT-4.1 models in Azure OpenAI are used to generate images based on natural language prompts.

**Learn more:** [What is the Whisper model?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/whisper-overview) · [Azure OpenAI Embeddings REST API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/microsoft-foundry/azureopenai/embeddings)

finalExplanation: Whisper performs speech-to-text transcription. Embedding models produce vector representations of text for similarity and semantic-search workloads. GPT-4.1 supports text and image processing, but dedicated image-generation models are used to create images from prompts.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a chatbot that will use natural language processing (NLP) to carry out the following actions from a user's text input:  
  
- Accept customer orders.  
- Retrieve support documents.  
- Retrieve order-status updates.  
  
Which type of NLP should you use?
definition.explanation:
Language understanding identifies the intent expressed in a user's text, allowing a conversational application to distinguish requests to place an order, retrieve support content, or obtain an order-status update and route each request to the appropriate action. It can also extract relevant details needed to fulfill that intent.

**Learn more:** [Conversational Language Understanding overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/conversational-language-understanding/overview) · [Build, train, and deploy a conversational language understanding model](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/conversational-language-understanding/how-to/build-train-deploy-model)

finalExplanation: Language understanding identifies the intent expressed in a user's text, allowing a conversational application to distinguish requests to place an order, retrieve support content, or obtain an order-status update and route each request to the appropriate action. It can also extract relevant details needed to fulfill that intent.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a lightweight application that will call an agent programmatically by using the Microsoft Foundry SDK.  
  
You need to determine the agent ID.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the model catalog, open the model card and copy the model family name.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the Foundry portal, copy the project name.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the Foundry tool catalog, copy the tool name used by the agent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the Foundry playground, select Code, and view the .env variables.

definition.explanation:
An agent ID is the unique identifier required to target a specific agent in a programmatic SDK call. The Foundry playground's generated Code view exposes the agent configuration as environment variables, allowing the application to use that identifier; model-family, project, and tool names do not uniquely identify the agent.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Get started with Microsoft Foundry SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/quickstarts/get-started-code?tabs=portal&view=foundry)

finalExplanation: An agent ID is the unique identifier required to target a specific agent in a programmatic SDK call. The Foundry playground's generated Code view exposes the agent configuration as environment variables, allowing the application to use that identifier; model-family, project, and tool names do not uniquely identify the agent.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building an application that continuously transcribes speech from a default microphone by using Azure Speech in Microsoft Foundry Tools.  
  
You need to carry out speech-to-text transcription from the microphone.

**Learn more:** [SpeechRecognizer Class — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/azure-cognitiveservices-speech/azure.cognitiveservices.speech.speechrecognizer?view=azure-python) · [Speech-to-text quickstart — Foundry Tools | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/get-started-speech-to-text)

finalExplanation: `SpeechRecognizer` performs speech-to-text recognition and supports continuous recognition. It can be constructed with an audio configuration that uses the default microphone; `SpeechConfig` configures the service, while the synthesizer and audio-output configuration are for speech output.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an AI solution that processes customer information.  
  
Which task exemplifies the Microsoft responsible AI principle of privacy and security?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encrypt stored customer data and restrict system access by using role-based controls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Provide explanations about how the system generates predictions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Test the system under unexpected conditions to prevent harmful failures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Evaluate model outputs across demographic groups to reduce bias.

definition.explanation:
Encrypting stored customer data and enforcing role-based access controls protect sensitive information from unauthorized access, directly supporting privacy and security. Microsoft guidance describes encryption of customer content at rest and role-based access control as data-protection measures.

**Learn more:** [Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployoffice/privacy/microsoft-365-copilot)

finalExplanation: Encrypting stored customer data and enforcing role-based access controls protect sensitive information from unauthorized access, directly supporting privacy and security. Microsoft guidance describes encryption of customer content at rest and role-based access control as data-protection measures.

definition.stemRaw:
Match responsible-AI principles with the appropriate requirements.  
  
A principle may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

slots.label: The system must not discriminate based on gender, race, or age.
Personal data must be visible only to approved users.
Automated decision-making processes must be recorded so that approved users can identify why a decision was made.

definition.explanation:
Fairness requires AI systems to avoid systematic bias and disparate treatment of comparable people. Privacy and security protect personal information through appropriate data boundaries and access controls. Transparency requires decision-making to be understandable and reviewable, so decision records that reveal why an automated decision was made satisfy this principle.

**Learn more:** [What is Responsible AI? - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/concept-responsible-ai?view=azureml-api-2)

finalExplanation: Fairness requires AI systems to avoid systematic bias and disparate treatment of comparable people. Privacy and security protect personal information through appropriate data boundaries and access controls. Transparency requires decision-making to be understandable and reviewable, so decision records that reveal why an automated decision was made satisfy this principle.

statements.text: A summarization model is used to transcribe spoken audio into written text.
A chat completion model can generate vector embeddings for semantic tasks.
An embedding model can generate vector representations of the provided input.

definition.explanation:
Summarization produces concise representations of text or conversations; it is not speech-to-text transcription. Chat-completion models return generated chat messages, while embedding models create numeric vectors for semantic comparison tasks such as search, clustering, and recommendations. Embedding APIs return a vector representing the supplied input.

**Learn more:** [Generate embeddings with Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/embeddings) · [Work with chat completion models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/chatgpt)

Chat-completion models return generated chat messages, while embedding models create numeric vectors for semantic comparison tasks such as search, clustering, and recommendations. Embedding APIs return a vector representing the supplied input.
